findings.claim: The requirement says MessagePack attributes on T must be honoured. When no SurrogateType is set, `Collect` always calls `CreateContractlessMembers(type)`, and that method never reads T's attributes. Two inputs show the problem. First, a referenced `[MessagePackObject] class AnnotatedType { [Key(0)] int Visible; [IgnoreMember] int IgnoredSecret; }` still has `IgnoredSecret` serialized. Second, T's integer `[Key]` indexes are discarded: the type is written as a string-keyed map (alphabetical by name) instead of an array. `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]` are ignored in the same way.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterLogicReceipts.ReferencedTypeIgnoreMemberIsHonoured and ReferencedTypeIntKeysAreHonoured. Each emits a referenced ProjectA type with [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember], runs the generator for `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class XFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.X>`, and asserts on the generated formatter text. On head the text contains IgnoredSecret and uses WriteMapHeader rather than WriteArrayHeader.

findings.claim: `IsPartial` only checks the formatter's own declaration. The FormatterTemplate/StringKeyFormatterTemplate now emit the user formatter through `EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces` with `Formatter = new QualifiedNamedTypeName(formatter)`. As a result, a formatter nested in a non-partial containing class (`public class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] internal partial class PayloadFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<Payload> {} }`) passes validation. The generator then emits code that does not compile (CS0260 missing partial on Outer, or CS0535 unimplemented members) instead of reporting MsgPack019.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterLogicReceipts.FormatterNestedInNonPartialTypeIsDiagnosedInsteadOfEmittingBrokenCode. It runs the generator on a nested formatter in a non-partial Outer and asserts that either an MsgPack diagnostic is reported or the output compilation has no errors. On head there is no MsgPack diagnostic and the output has compile errors.

findings.claim: Classes with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] are now excluded from the hand-written formatter set, which is what TypeCollector uses as KnownFormatters/custom-formatter precedence. If T is declared in the same compilation with [MessagePackObject], TypeCollector no longer sees that T has a custom formatter. It therefore also generates its own formatter for T, and the resolver registers two ObjectSerializationInfos for the same DataType: the user's formatter and the generated <T>Formatter. On base, a hand-written formatter suppressed the generated one.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a source with `[MessagePackObject] public class MyObject { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} }`, `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class MyObjectFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject> {}` and `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class R {}`. Inspect the generated resolver for two registrations of typeof(global::MyObject), then call R.Instance.GetFormatter<MyObject>() at run time to check for a duplicate-key type initializer failure or for the wrong formatter being returned.
